- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.5) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.2) or shows strong reversal — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Lagged price spikes (e.g., 3–5 day highs) are often over-predicted in the 30-day forecast — model reacts too slowly to new highs.
- Mean reversion bias: if recent 18-day average is high, model often forecasts higher than true outcome — especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves: if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often forecasts peak too early and too high.
- Sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment is consistently positive, model tends to overfit upward trend; when sentiment turns negative, model underreacts to correction.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overestimating late-period price action (last 7–10 days) — true outcome often dips after initial spike.
